course_name_original: Técnicas de Expresión Oral y Escrita en Inglés
course_name_en: Oral and Written Expression Techniques in English
prerequisites: Prior knowledge of English grammatical and linguistic structures
Communicative competence at B2 level according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages

learning_outcomes.text: Follow and deliver simple oral presentations, making correct use of intonation and expressive possibilities.
Request and offer services related to the work environment, using varied, precise, and appropriate vocabulary for the situation in question.
Participate in meetings and seminars by taking notes, expressing own ideas, and making proposals.
Handle routine requests for goods or services over the phone.
Draft and comprehend formal reports and usual professional correspondence in accordance with established rhetorical, grammatical, and lexical norms.

syllabus_topics: Preparation of technical reports: structure and linguistic characteristics
Participating in socio-professional activities within the company context:
Conducting job interviews and CV presentations
Participating in debates, meetings, and negotiations
Use of language and linguistic signaling techniques
Use of visual aids and body language
Use of voice: rhythm and emphasis

assessment_methods.method: Partial exam (E1) - written exam on a cover letter
Practical work (T1) - submission of individual Curriculum Vitae
Partial exam (E2) - individual oral exam on a simulated job interview
Practical work (T2) - written technical report by two or more students
Partial exam (E3) - written exam on the technical report (linguistic and content aspects)
Partial exam (E4) - group debate participation (individually assessed)
Partial exam (E5) - individual oral presentation on technological innovation
Class participation (C1) - active participation in practical sessions

assessment_rules: For the ordinary assessment, the final grade is calculated as the sum of E1 + T1 + E2 + T2 + E3 + E4 + E5 + E6 + C1. A minimum score of 5 out of 10 is required to pass the subject. For class participation (C1), a minimum attendance of 80% to practical sessions is required to receive a grade. For extraordinary examinations, students will take a theoretical exam (P1, P2, P3, P4) and a practical exam (T1), with no previous grades carried over. The final grade is calculated as P1+P2+P3+P4+T1, and a minimum score of 5 out of 10 is required to pass. Fraudulent use of sources, AI, and/or plagiarism will result in a 0/10 grade for the affected activity.
